bull_bear.body: Disciplined greenfield expansion in underserved Eastern/Central markets; 90% of Jamshedpur capex deployed in FY27; Evaluating M&A for 150-200 bed assets; No dividend commentary provided.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raipur ramp-up delay beyond Q3FY27 breakeven target; Insurance empanelment delays (critical for Raipur volume); Staff attrition due to new competitor entry in Raipur; Bangladesh geopolitical/visa volatility impacting Agartala volumes; West Bengal election aftermath impact on scheme patients (minimal expected).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural demand in Eastern India; Pragmatic on Raipur losses (temporary); Aggressive on specialty mix upgrades (robotics, transplants); Clear on 24-36 month breakeven cycle for new assets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Raipur's current high ARPOB is artificial due to lack of insurance empanelment (cash-heavy mix); margins may normalize lower as insurance mix rises; Dumdum's turnaround was driven by decentralizing specialty focus rather than just marketing; Agartala has latent 100-bed expansion capacity on existing land unused until 70% occupancy hit.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt to equity is negative across the deck's series: -0.12 (FY24), -0.09 (FY25), -0.12 (FY26); the deck describes the company as net-debt free.
- Stated goal of maintaining long-term ROE and ROCE of ~25% alongside ongoing enhancements in care quality; deck's ROE/ROCE series are labelled 2024/2025/2026 with values ROE 21.8, 28.1, 16.5 and ROCE 20.1, 23.5, 15.7 (chart binding of the two series to years is only partially legible in extraction).
- Reinvestment is directed at capacity (1,000 beds) and clinical technology, deliberately through asset-light/developer-funded formats to limit balance-sheet strain.
- The deck makes no statement on dividend policy or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic presence in Eastern India with underpenetrated healthcare markets and persistent demand-supply gaps
- Enhanced brand equity through well-located hospitals in densely populated areas under the ILS Hospitals brand
- Skilled medical workforce and high-volume tertiary care model (115 full-time and 630 visiting consultants)
- Early-mover advantage and strong medical professional network in the region
- Digital transformation via HMIS and an interconnected digital ecosystem (Salesforce, LeadSquared, SAP) for seamless patient experience
- Integrated diagnostics and affordable, accessible care positioning
- Net debt-free / low-leverage balance sheet supporting asset-light expansion
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Low bed occupancy — Suboptimal inpatient utilisation relative to peers may limit revenue and dilute returns on capital investments; FY26 blended occupancy was 45.9% and several hospitals (notably the newly commissioned Raipur) run well below mature-hospital levels.
- Supply chain dependency — Dependence on third-party suppliers for medical consumables and equipment may disrupt operations if vendors fail to meet obligations.
- Revenue / payor concentration — Over-reliance on a narrow mix of revenue streams or payor segments could amplify the impact of any adverse development.
- Payment delays from insurers — Delayed reimbursements from insurers and third-party payors may constrain cash flow and affect financial stability.
- Regulatory & licensing changes — Changes to healthcare regulations or accreditation standards may require operational adjustments and increase compliance costs.
- Cybersecurity breach / data privacy — Unauthorised access to patient or financial data could result in regulatory penalties, reputational harm and operational disruption; non-compliance with health data privacy laws (including the DPDP Act, 2023) could attract penalties and erode patient trust.
- IT system failures — Failures in core clinical or administrative systems could disrupt operations, impact patient care, and compromise sensitive data.
- Talent attraction and retention — Need for continuous adaptation to rapid medical technology change and challenges in attracting and retaining skilled medical professionals, flagged as a threat in the Company's SWOT analysis.

business.body:
- Described as a hospital platform in Eastern India operating five neighbourhood tertiary-care hospitals located within densely populated residential areas, a proximity-based model offering advanced care "almost at the doorstep" while enabling control over clinical quality, operating standards and long-term returns on capital.
- Key investment proposition claims Eastern India market leadership through regional brand equity, and strategic locations in dense residential areas near transport hubs for easy patient access; Howrah is stated to have no competing hospital within a 5-km radius.
- High-quality payor mix: the deck targets "over 90% revenue from cash and insured patients, ensuring minimal dependence on Govt schemes or Corporates".
- Agartala is stated to be the only private hospital in Tripura accredited by both NABH and NABL, with clinical leadership in the state and evolution into a medical value travel hub attracting international patients.
- Pricing is calibrated for "high-quality, accessible care for middle-to-high income segments", driving volume growth while protecting margins.

- [Leadership] Led by founder Dr. Om Tantia, Chairman & Managing Director, a founding member of ILS Hospitals with 40+ years as a medical practitioner; board includes several Tantia family members plus independent directors.

- [Industry framing] Deck cites an INR 99,858 crore government healthcare outlay, India's ~3 million bed shortfall, medical tourism in Eastern India from Bangladesh/Nepal/Bhutan, and hospital sector valuations of 20x-30x EBITDA.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Lift occupancy across mature hospitals (Salt Lake, Agartala, Dum Dum, Howrah) past the 70% mark through disciplined capacity utilisation and equipment optimisation
- Scale the network toward a 1,000-bed target within two years through expansion into Tier I and Tier II markets in Eastern India
- Deepen investment in robotic surgery and renal and cardiac sciences as part of a technology-enabled, next-generation care platform
- Maintain a balanced, doctor-agnostic, broad specialty mix with a diversified case mix that allows new services to be introduced in response to demand
- Continue growing on an asset-light, net-debt-free footing, executing new capacity addition via asset-light rental models to limit balance sheet strain
- Strengthen existing hospitals by expanding specialty mix, deepening expertise, and introducing new services
- Explore asset-light expansion via revenue-sharing and management-based models to accelerate growth with minimal operational risk
- Optimise hospital efficiency by increasing occupancy rates, improving equipment utilisation, and expanding tertiary care, preventive healthcare and community outreach programmes
- Adopt advanced medical technologies, including robotic-assisted surgery, to strengthen clinical capabilities
- Evaluate further greenfield and acquisition opportunities across underserved markets in Uttar Pradesh, Assam and Odisha, and select Tier I locations in Eastern India
- Dividend payouts are proposed by the Board as an interim dividend (paid during the year) and a final dividend, with the final dividend subject to shareholder confirmation/declaration at the Annual General Meeting; the FY26 AGM notice includes confirmation of the interim dividend already paid and declaration of the final dividend for the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is building its sixth hospital, a 155-bed tertiary care facility at Adityapur, Jamshedpur (Jharkhand) under the ILS Hospitals brand, with an MoU signed at a project outlay of approximately Rs.75 crore; commissioning is targeted for Q4 FY27 (on track per the Annual Report), taking total planned network capacity to 874 beds, with roughly 90% of the project capex to be deployed in the current year. The Company's fifth hospital, ILS Raipur (158 beds, Pachpedi Naka, Chhattisgarh), was commissioned in May 2025, marking its first entry into Central India; it remains in a ramp-up/investment phase (reporting an EBITDA loss during FY26) with renal transplant, chemotherapy, oncology and liver-transplant services being rolled out, and management expects it to reach monthly EBITDA breakeven within 6-8 months of commissioning (referenced elsewhere as Q3 FY27). Beyond Jamshedpur, the Company is in the process of closing on a seventh hospital, which would take total bed count to 1,000+, and has identified further greenfield/acquisition entry points in Tier II cities of Uttar Pradesh, Assam and Odisha as well as select Tier I locations in Eastern India. New capacity is being added under an asset-light rental model, which the Company states reduces capital commitment per bed and enables faster deployment into new geographies.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's hospital bed density remains at approximately 1.3 beds per 1,000 people, well below global averages and even more pronounced across Eastern and Central India, indicating a large structural demand-supply gap
- Rising disposable incomes, deepening insurance penetration, and growing demand for organised, technology-led tertiary care are expected to support sector growth
- Government commitment to healthcare remains strong, with a near-Rs.1,00,000 crore (Rs.99,858 crore cited) healthcare outlay channelled through Ayushman Bharat, the National Health Mission and PM-ABHIM expanding both demand and capacity
- Eastern India is emerging as a medical value travel corridor for international patients from Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan; India's MVT market is projected to reach $16.2 billion by 2030, and the Company's Bangladesh patient segment has begun recovering after a period of disruption
- India's ageing population, with median age projected to reach 38.3 by 2050, is expected to underpin sustained structural demand for specialised, chronic and tertiary hospital services
- Growing digital adoption is enabling hospital apps to deliver telemedicine, AI-assisted diagnostics and remote monitoring, lowering costs and extending reach beyond physical catchments
- Indian healthcare industry projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 6.31%, supported by rising healthcare awareness, insurance penetration, expanding medical infrastructure and demand for specialised care; sector transitioning from volume-driven to value-driven care
- Rising incidence of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) is driving demand for specialised tertiary care services, with strong growth in complex, high-acuity treatments across cardiology, oncology, nephrology and robotic surgery
- Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are increasingly emerging as healthcare growth centres due to infrastructure expansion and improving accessibility
- Company profitability was moderated in FY26 versus FY25 primarily due to the ramp-up costs of the newly added Raipur hospital (higher depreciation and interest cost); management expects continued focus on optimising hospital utilisation and expanding specialty services to support long-term growth and improved financial performance
- Policy enablers flagged as still-limited but potentially additive: strengthening public health infrastructure, improving insurance penetration, expanding Ayushman Bharat, GST exemption on health insurance premiums, and increased health-related Union Budget allocations
- MoU signed for the Company's sixth hospital, a 155-bed facility in Jamshedpur (Adityapur), at a project outlay of Rs.75 crore, taking total planned network capacity to 874 beds
- Company is in the process of closing on a seventh hospital, which would take the total bed count to 1,000+
- Company has identified planned entry points into Tier II cities in Uttar Pradesh, Assam and Odisha, as well as select Tier I locations in Eastern India, for future greenfield/acquisition-led expansion
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
